description:
pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs:305

The trait method check_revocation_against_anchor lacks #[must_use]. Clippy pedantic flags this as 'docs for function returning Result missing # Errors section' (companion issue), but the more pressing concern is that unlike check_revocation (which already has #[must_use] at line 273), check_revocation_against_anchor does not.

A caller who calls this method and discards the Result will silently skip anchor-level revocation checking with no warning. The security doc already calls this out as a silent security gap; enforcing #[must_use] at the trait level makes the omission a compile-time error rather than a runtime surprise.

  #[must_use = "revocation check result must not be silently discarded"]
  fn check_revocation_against_anchor(
      &self,
      _cert: &Certificate,
      _anchor: &TrustAnchor,
  ) -> crate::Result<()>
title: [rusty] pkix-revocation: RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor missing #[must_use]
